instruction: Add two tab stops to every paragraph in the document: a left-aligned one at the start (0 cm) and a right-aligned one at 15 cm.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the .docx file and extracts tab stops from each non-empty paragraph via para.paragraph_format.tab_stops, which captures tabs set directly on paragraphs (the expected workflow for Format > Paragraph > Tabs in LibreOffice Writer).
Alignment enum parsing (splitting on '.' to get 'LEFT'/'RIGHT') correctly handles python-docx WD_TAB_ALIGNMENT enum string representation.
Metric checks both required tab stops (left at ~0 cm, right at ~15 cm) per paragraph, exactly matching the instruction.
Partial credit design (0.5 per tab per paragraph, averaged over all paragraphs) is appropriate and correctly handles the 'every paragraph' requirement.
Negative control resistance is correct: initial document state has no tab stops, so score is 0.0.
left_aligns={'LEFT','START'} and right_aligns={'RIGHT','END'} cover the relevant python-docx alignment enum variants.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The 0.5 cm tolerance for the 0 cm left tab is slightly permissive (accepts any tab from 0-0.5 cm); consider tightening to 0.1-0.2 cm for the left tab if strict position matching is desired.
If tab stops are applied via a paragraph style rather than directly on paragraphs, para.paragraph_format.tab_stops would miss them; this is unlikely given the expected UI workflow but worth noting.
